newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN BATSMEN AWAIT USE LOGO BATS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN BATSMEN AWAIT USE LOGO BATS.

text.p: Pakistan batsmen took to the crease wielding bats with tobacco sponsor logos on Friday in the face of an Australian government order to remove the slogans as they breach tobacco advertising laws.
The Pakistanis used the bats in their day-night match against West Indies in Brisbane, after the government on Thursday ordered their removal.
Pakistan team manager Yawar Saeed said the batsmen were awaiting orders from their cricket board before removing the sponsors' logo from their bats.
"I'm not the policy-maker so I will have to wait until I get the new instructions," Saeed told Australian radio, addding he had notified the Pakistan Cricket Board.
The Australian government has given Pakistan until Tuesday to remove the Wills Kings cigarette company slogan from bats.

The logos were visible on bats used by a number of Pakistan players during the touring team's four-wicket defeat of Australia in a World Series match in Sydney on Wednesday and again in Brisbane on Friday. Both the Sydney and Brisbane matches were televised around Australia and internationally.
The Australian government notified the Australian Cricket Board (ACB) of its decision on Thursday and it in turn notified the Pakistan manager.
Saeed said the ACB did not recommend any action.
"They (the ACB) are awaiting the response from the Pakistan Cricket Board," he said. The ACB faces a fine of A$60,000 (US$47,400) unless Pakistan removes the logos.
Saeed said he did not whether the Pakistan Cricket Board would comply with the order.
"If we knew that we were violating (advertising laws) we would not do it. We do not violate rules of our own country or any other country," he said.
"We will just continue doing what we are told to do."

Many of the Pakistan players, who are in Australia for the World Series limited overs tournament against Australia and West Indies, have stickers bearing the corporate logo and name of team sponsors Wills Kings, a Pakistani company which manufactures cricket equipment and cigarettes.

Tobacco adverts are banned at Australian sporting and cultural events unless an exemption is granted under the Tobacco Advertising Prohibition Act. The Formula One Grand Prix motor race in Victoria next March has such an exemption.
